notes: Rank 1 of the blind phenotype-driven pipeline. No gene panel, disease name or candidate list was supplied: the only human input was the 8 HPO terms from the clinical document. Resnik/best-match-average phenotype similarity ranked BUB1B 15th of 5268 annotated disease genes; variant evidence over the top 200 then isolated this pair as the single best-supported finding. BUB1B NM_001211.6 c.2210T>G p.Leu737Ter (nonsense, exon 17/23, NMD-predicted null, gnomAD 7.9e-05) with c.3006T>G p.Asn1002Lys (missense, exon 23/23, kinase domain, absent from gnomAD, deleterious by SIFT/PolyPhen-2/AlphaMissense). Consistent with Mosaic Variegated Aneuploidy type 1 (MIM 257300). Phase in trans not provable: the alleles are 10.9 kb apart, beyond short-read phasing, and GATK emits no shared PID for them.

Rank 3 of the same blind pipeline, retained for transparency of the automated output and NOT considered contributory. RAI1 p.Gln280AlafsTer. The pipeline initially proposed a RAI1 compound heterozygote from this variant plus chr17:17793787 AG>A, but GATK physical phasing rejects it: both calls carry PID 17793784_AGC_A with identical PGT 0|1, placing them in cis on one haplotype as two representations of a single complex indel, not two alleles. The surviving single call sits in a repetitive tract and the proband phenotype does not match RAI1 haploinsufficiency (Smith-Magenis syndrome).
